reviewer_summary: Manual synthesis after the deliberation was killed at end of round 3 due to wall-clock cost (~35 min for 3 rounds, ~7-8 min per position). Round 3 was already producing diminishing returns — both agents had converged on a substantive core with two narrow residual disagreements. The single highest-priority next improvement is a chassis-owned verifier/adjudicator stage that resolves cited evidence into a ledger and drives convergence from the ledger rather than from agents' self-reported agreed_with_peer / disagreed_with_peer. Both agents reached this conclusion independently by round 3 with file:line citations.

claims.claim: Highest-priority next improvement is a chassis-owned verifier/adjudicator stage. After each round, before convergence_check, run a non-LLM verifier that opens every claim's evidence_path, records verified|unresolved_path|content_mismatch|unparseable per claim, attaches the actual file content snippet, tracks claim lineage across rounds (rename / retire / fabricated peer ref detection), and feeds detect_convergence() the ledger instead of agents' self-reported metadata. Closes converged findings 1, 2, and partially 3.

Convergence detector is structurally weaker than 'polite agents trust' framing. agreed_with_peer is list[str] of free-text strings the same agent authored in the same response; detect_convergence treats them as a set; nothing prevents silent claim renames, silently retired claims, or fabricated peer IDs from passing the check. Set subset semantics also let extra-garbage agreed_with_peer entries pass.

evidence_path is a bare str with no sub-grammar — 'docs/x.md#sec', 'file.py:LL-LL', and 'because I said so' all pass schema validation. Even syntactic+filesystem-only verification is insufficient for v1 (agent can cite a real file:line with misstated content); v1 must attach actual content snippet from the cited range. LLM-semantic content match is a v2 question.

Round-1 non-independence is graph-deterministic and inconsistent with the docstring's 'each agent independently' framing. LangGraph edges hardwire agent_a -> agent_b -> round_increment, entry_point is agent_a, agent_a's position is written into latest_positions before agent_b reads. agent_b's round-1 prompt includes agent_a's round-1 position via the peer_latest block.

Synthesis is a distinct context-bloat failure mode from convergence drift. _synthesis_prompt dumps the full chronological position_history via json.dumps(positions, indent=2) into one LLM call with no truncation, summarization, or last-N-rounds limit. Bites at max_rounds > 5 before agent-prompt bloat does — per-round agent prompts only see peer_latest + own_prior, but synthesis sees everything.

Deliberation chassis is missing the TaskFamily/profile extension point the duet has, despite the module docstring promising 'deliberation can also be specialized by profile when domain-specific Position fields are needed'. Build-order resolution from round 3: verifier ships first but MUST include an override hook so future DeliberationFamily can plug in a domain-specific verifier without forking the chassis. Full DeliberationFamily registry can land later.

RECANTED (was originally agent_b's b1 highest-priority): max_budget is NOT reused as a per-call cap; the kernel layer's _check_budget loads cumulative spend by trace_id and WorkflowContext reuses one trace_id across every agent/synthesis call. Earlier framing of budget-cap leakage was wrong; this is a corrected mental model, not a bug.

open_questions: Does an LLM-semantic content match (does the cited snippet actually support the claim) need to ship in v1 of the verifier, or is filesystem+snippet-attachment sufficient as a v1 floor?
Should claim_id become chassis-owned (stable IDs across rounds, monotonic across the run) rather than agent-authored free text, so lineage tracking is structurally guaranteed?
Is the verifier stage best implemented inside the deliberation chassis only, or should it also gate the duet's reviewer schemas (PlanReviewBlocker.evidence_path, CorrectnessFinding.file_path+line)?

disagreed_with_peer.my_counterclaim: Narrow build-order residual: A prefers adjudicator-first then extension hook in a separate change; B prefers verifier-with-override-hook in the same change. Engineering preference, not a structural disagreement. Either ordering works.

B claims silent-claim-retirement detection must be an explicit named requirement of the adjudicator. A claims it falls out naturally from lineage tracking. Equivalent in outcome; framing difference only. Implementation should make the silent-retirement detection observable in the per-claim ledger output so the property is testable.
